name: Foreman's Blackjack
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Foreman's Blackjack keeps Durotar's peons at work. Foremen use the leather-wrapped cosh to wake laborers who fall asleep during the Horde's early construction.

sections.title: A Tool of Orcish Labor
sections.body: Durotar needs stockpiles of lumber for the Horde's new home. In the Valley of Trials, peons do the work, and Foreman Thazz'ril keeps the crews moving with Foreman's Blackjack. Its weighted blow jolts laborers awake when they nap beneath the valley's shade trees. It is meant to wake them, not kill them. Peon life in the new Horde means hard, unglamorous work under an iron fist.

faq.q: What is the Foreman's Blackjack used for?
faq.answer: Overseers give the blackjack to young adventurers to discipline sleeping peons in the Valley of Trials. A strike jolts a napping peon awake, and they return to chopping and hauling wood.
Foreman Thazz'ril owns the blackjack. The labor taskmaster is stationed in the Valley of Trials, where he oversees the collection of raw timber for the young Orc settlement.

faq.q: Why do the peons keep falling asleep on the job?
faq.answer: Orcish peons work exhausting shifts gathering wood under Durotar's harsh sun. When exhaustion overtakes them, they often nap without permission beneath the valley's sparse trees.

faq.q: Can I keep the blackjack after finishing the task?
faq.answer: No. The overseer demands the tool back as soon as the shirkers have been disciplined. It stays with taskmasters who enforce labor quotas.

angles.text: For young orcs entering the Valley of Trials, wielding the blackjack offers an early lesson in Horde hierarchy. Those without a warrior's strength or spirit are sent to labor and kept in line by force.
The blackjack reflects the work needed to tame Durotar. Settling this harsh land requires every laborer to work without pause.
